asset_sourcing.note: Try scripts/find_reference_images.py (Wikimedia Commons / NASA Images / Archive.org, PD/CC0/CC-BY/CC-BY-SA only - M09 §8b) BEFORE generating a Flow prompt for a scene. A real archival photograph/footage clip of the actual historical subject is not just cheaper than an AI illustration of it, it's a stronger claim for rights.source_basis: "public_domain" - an evidenced fact from source_url, not an inference. Flow generation remains the fallback for any scene find_reference_images.py can't resolve (no reusably-licensed candidate found), same fallback_to_still pattern already used for flow_account_pool exhaustion. This field has no dedicated schema slot in template.schema.json - additionalProperties: true carries it; promote to a real schema field if a second template needs the same shape.

source_note: Identical director/visual/audio to TPL-documentary (its parent) - the only real difference this template encodes is asset_sourcing.priority putting archival footage before Flow generation. budget_profile.credits_per_minute is roughly halved (180 -> 90) versus TPL-documentary as a planning estimate, not a measured constant (unlike TPL-archaeological-documentary's wpm=115, which IS a measured value from a delivered project) - a scene resolved via find_reference_images.py costs a curl download, not a Flow generation credit, so a project leaning heavily on archival sourcing should spend markedly less per minute than one that doesn't; recalibrate this number once a real project using this template has delivered footage to measure against, same discipline TPL-archaeological-documentary's own source_note follows.
